Chapter 10 — Neural Networks (notes)

Source: https://natureofcode.com/neural-networks/

Summary:
Chapter 10 introduces neural networks as computational systems inspired by the
brain’s network of neurons. Key ideas:
- Neural networks learn from data by adjusting connection strengths between
  artificial neurons.
- A neuron computes a weighted sum of inputs, applies an activation function,
  and passes output to the next layer.
- Layers: input layer, hidden layers, and output layer. Deeper networks can
  represent more complex functions.
- Training uses error-driven learning to change weights; common methods include
  gradient descent and backpropagation.
- Neural networks can make decisions, classify patterns, and approximate
  continuous functions.
